chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari from Mu'alla from Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Hashimi who said: My father narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa who said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to me from his father from his grandfather from Ali (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says:

To the son of Adam: If your eye disputes with you regarding some of what I have prohibited to you, then I have aided you against it with two layers (eyelids), so close them and do not look. And if your tongue disputes with you regarding some of what I have prohibited to you, then I have aided you against it with two layers (lips), so close them and do not speak. And if your genitals dispute with you regarding some of what I have prohibited to you, then I have aided you against it with two layers (legs), so close them and do not come to the prohibited.

key_terms.بَطْنَيْنِ: Two layers (referring to eyelids, lips, or legs)

ai.seo_question: How does God help humans control their desires according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith qudsi from al-Kafi elucidates the physiological mechanism of 'tabaqayn' (two layers) as divine aids for restraining the faculties of sight, speech, and procreation, emphasizing that God facilitates self-control. It underscores the Shia ethical principle that physical restraint is a cooperative act with divine grace, urging believers to actively seal these senses against transgression. The teaching highlights the holistic nature of human nature, where bodily mechanisms are not merely biological but spiritual tools for moral discipline.
